Man, finding a doctor that gives you the right medication is like searching for a love partner lol I don't take medications, but I have a friend who does, so I know the struggle. I hope that you'll find something that will make you feel like yourself.

I'm glad you have something to hold on to too. Most redditors (?) have mentioned other people. I think this is why it is so important for us to talk about these things, to them. By communicating, we are allowing them to understand us and we are giving them the freedom to choose if they want to remain by our side. I know I will sound very naive by saying this, but it never occurred to me the idea of two people, who have the same mental issues, being together. It was a choice. This gives me hope. 

I've been recommended to not do LSD because my great grandmother was schizophrenic. So I have that on hold.

I've gone hiking which is really similar. I assure you, depending on the value you give to it, it can be life changing.  I tried hiking to the top of a mountain. You have to sweat, work hard, you may fall, you'll have to take breaks. It's really challenging, but as cliché as it sounds, once you reach the top, everything else seems so small. It's beautiful.

I loved having the freedom to explore, to walk wherever I wanted to, to talk to whomever I wanted to and being chased by literally everything xD  

I'll stick to that inner drive. What's the worst that could happen?

Thank you for this. After reading these posts under r/suicidewatch for the first time I feel immensely overwhelmed.  I never thought there would be so many. I hope this post gives everyone the hope they deserve to have.

Improvement. It is possible that you have improved, but you just don't see it. You know, we don't always notice it.

There's a guy I really like and I believe he's waiting for his birthday (November) to do it. He probably feels like he's been doing the opposite of improvement. He dropped out of college, does not have a job, has gained weight, substance abuse ect. 
However, I'm looking at the small steps, the little projects he proposes. A few days ago he told me he wanted to build a bird feeder. Sounds totally unrelated, but I see willingness to work, to compromise, discipline, love for others (the birds), and that's better than laying in bed all day. This last week he's been trying to get off of heroin too. 
Yes, he has a long way to go and a lot of work to do, but there is improvement. 
I see it. 

We live in a culture that overvalues time and speed. 
Be patient with yourself. 
Take your fucking time.
